previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with ongoing abdominal pain that worsened after eating, consistent with an acute on chronic flare. She had been on TPN since a recent admission but experienced increased pain after oral intake. Lipase and liver enzymes were normal, and MRCP showed chronic pancreatitis changes with stable pancreatic cysts, no acute inflammation. She remained on TPN and was managed with IV then oral pain medications, including an increase in her fentanyl patch to 100 mcg/hour. Pain improved with minimal oral intake. Iron deficiency anemia was confirmed with a ferritin of 9.8, and outpatient plans were made for colonoscopy and possible IV iron. Constipation, worsened by narcotics, was treated with increased bowel regimen. She was discharged home on TPN with visiting nurse services, follow-up arranged with GI, and instructions for repeat pancreatic imaging in 12 months.

radiology_notes.text:
PATIENT HISTORY:  ___ woman with new onset fevers and reflux, assess
for pneumonia or aspiration.

COMPARISON: Chest x-ray ___.

FINDINGS:  New right lower lobe opacity is compatible with aspiration
pneumonia.  Lung is otherwise clear.  There is no pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. Wedge deformities of
the lower thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:  New right lower lobe opacity is suspicious for aspiration
pneumonia.

HISTORY:  ___ -year-old female requiring TPN 

COMPARISON:  PICC line placement ___.  

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___, present and supervising throughout the
procedure, Dr. ___ fellow)

FLUOROSCOPY:  Total fluoro time 7.17 min, 27 mGy.  10 cc of Optiray 320 used. 


PROCEDURE:

Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the patent and compressible
right brachial vein was accessed using a micropuncture needle ultrasound
guidance, and an 018 wire was inserted, however could not be passed beyond the
subclavian vein.  The inner dilator of the micropuncture system was inserted
into the vein, and a brief venogram demonstrated a tight central subclavian
vein stenosis.  Multiple attempts to cross the stenosis with a long Nitinol
wire and 018 glidewire were unsuccessful.  

The patient was repositioned on the fluoroscopy table and the left arm was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Access to the left basilic
vein was obtained under ultrasound guidance and an 018 wire was easily passed
into the superior vena cava.  The estimated measurement for the catheter was
44 cm.   Digital images were stored before and after ultrasound access.  

A peel-away sheath was then placed over the guidewire in the left basilic vein
and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 40 cm in length was then placed through
the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic
guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot image
of the chest.  

Peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was secured to
the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing was applied.  

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.  

FINDINGS:

Severe right subclavian stenosis preventing passage of an 018 wire from the
right arm access.

IMPRESSION:

Severe right subclavian stenosis precluding right arm PICC access at this
time.

Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 5 ___ double-lumen
PICC line placement via the left basilic venous approach.  Final internal
length is 44 cm with the tip positioned in the SVC.  The line is ready to use.
